title: AMERICAN EXPRESS 2022 Form 10-K — Table 4: Expenses Summary (p49)
key_points: FY2022 total expenses rose 24% (+$7,985M) YoY; FY2021 rose 22% (+$6,049M) YoY.

Other expenses increased primarily due to net losses on Amex Ventures investments in the current year versus net gains in the prior year.

title: AMERICAN EXPRESS 2022 Form 10-K — Business Environment (p45)
key_points: AMEX attributes the FY2022 net income decline ($8.1B to $7.5B) to credit reserve builds plus net losses in the Amex Ventures strategic investment portfolio, versus sizeable credit reserve releases and significant net gains in the prior year.
Provisions for credit losses increased YoY, reflecting a reserve build of $617M in FY2022 compared with a reserve release of $2.5B in FY2021.
Total revenues net of interest expense increased 25% YoY (27% FX-adjusted), reflecting strong growth in all revenue lines.
Discount revenue, the largest revenue line, increased 25% YoY driven by Card Member spending volume momentum.
Net card fees increased 17% YoY as new card acquisitions reached record levels in 2022.
Service fees and other revenues increased 36% YoY, driven in part by higher travel-related revenues.
Net interest income increased 28% YoY, primarily driven by growth in Card Member loans.
Billed business represented 86% of total network volumes and increased 23% YoY (25% FX-adjusted).
T&E spending momentum remained strong throughout the year, while YoY Goods & Services spending growth slowed toward the end of the year.
Inflation was a modest contributor to billed business growth; the strengthening U.S. dollar had a negative impact on international billings.
Card Member loans increased 22% YoY, with the majority of growth coming from existing Card Members.

title: AMERICAN EXPRESS 2022 Form 10-K — Business Environment: expense drivers and capital return (p46)
key_points: Card Member rewards, Card Member services and Business development expenses are generally correlated to volumes or variable based on usage, and increased YoY due to network volume growth and higher usage of travel-related benefits.
Card Member rewards expense growth was also driven by a larger proportion of billed business in categories that earn incremental rewards such as travel.

Operating expenses increased 24% YoY, primarily driven by net losses on Amex Ventures equity investments in the current year versus net gains in the prior year, plus higher compensation costs from an increased colleague base.
AMEX states it remains focused on driving marketing and operating expense efficiencies while continuing to invest in its growth strategy.
AMEX returned $4.9B of capital to shareholders in FY2022 through common share repurchases and dividends while keeping CET1 within its 10-11% target range.
AMEX expected to increase the regular quarterly common dividend by 15% beginning with the first quarter 2023 dividend declaration.

title: American Express 2022 10-K — Glossary of Selected Terminology: Adjusted net interest income (p85)
key_points: 公司将 'Adjusted net interest income' 定义为非 GAAP 指标：代表归属于卡会员贷款的净利息收入（GAAP 下包含被视为不可收回的利息），并剔除与卡会员贷款无关的利息费用与利息收入影响。
该定义确认 AMEX 在盈利分析中区分'归属于卡会员贷款的净利息收入'与'其他利息收支'，即净息差类指标是其分析框架的一部分。
raw_excerpt: Adjusted net interest income — A non-GAAP measure that represents net interest income attributable to our Card Member loans (which includes, on a GAAP basis, interest that is deemed uncollectible), excluding the impact of interest expense and interest income not attributable to our Card Member loans.

title: American Express 2022 Form 10-K — MD&A, Expenses discussion (variable/volume-correlated cost base)
key_points: AMEX states that Card Member rewards, Card Member services and Business development expenses are generally correlated to volumes or variable based on usage.
AMEX attributes the increase in those expense lines to network volume growth and higher usage of travel-related benefits.
Card Member rewards expense growth was additionally driven by a larger proportion of spend in categories that earn incremental rewards.
The Membership Rewards Ultimate Redemption Rate (URR) for current program participants was 96 percent (rounded down) at both December 31, 2022 and 2021.
raw_excerpt: Card Member rewards, Card Member services and Business development expenses are generally correlated to volumes or are variable based on usage, and increased year-over year due to network volume growth and higher usage of travel-related benefits.

title: American Express 2022 Form 10-K — MD&A, Business Environment (drivers of the 2022 net income decline)
key_points: AMEX states its business is 'in an even stronger position today than before the pandemic', with record network spending and credit metrics below pre-pandemic levels.
Total revenues net of interest expense increased 25% year-over-year (27% on an FX-adjusted basis) in 2022.
Worldwide network volumes increased 21% (24% FX-adjusted) and billed business increased 23% (25% FX-adjusted) in 2022.

The reduction in 2022 net income versus 2021 reflected credit reserve builds and net losses in the Amex Ventures strategic investment portfolio, versus sizeable credit reserve releases and significant net gains in the prior year.
Provisions for credit losses in 2022 reflected a reserve build of $617 million compared with a reserve release of $2.5 billion in the prior year.
Card Member loans increased 22% year-over-year in 2022.
raw_excerpt: Our results for the year demonstrate that our growth strategy is working and our business is in an even stronger position today than before the pandemic. Spending on our network reached record levels, and credit metrics remain below pre-pandemic levels. … The reduction in net income reflected credit reserve builds and net losses in our Amex Ventures strategic investment portfolio in the current year compared with sizeable credit reserve releases and significant net gains in our Amex Ventures strategic investment portfolio in the prior year.

title: American Express 2022 Form 10-K — MD&A, capital return and forward commitments (CET1 target range, dividend increase)
key_points: AMEX returned $4.9 billion of capital to shareholders through common share repurchases and dividend payments in 2022.
AMEX states it maintains its CET1 capital ratio within a target range of 10 to 11 percent.
AMEX expects to increase the regular quarterly dividend on common shares by 15 percent beginning with the first quarter 2023 dividend declaration.
AMEX states it plans to continue returning excess capital to shareholders while managing CET1 within its target range and supporting balance sheet growth.
The filing states no numeric 2023 revenue or EPS guidance and no long-term EPS or revenue growth target.
raw_excerpt: we returned $4.9 billion of capital to our shareholders through common share repurchases and dividend payments, while maintaining our Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) capital ratio within our target range of 10 to 11 percent. We plan to continue to return to shareholders the excess capital we generate, while managing our CET1 capital ratio within our target range and supporting balance sheet growth. We also expect to increase the regular quarterly dividend on common shares outstanding by 15 percent beginning with the first quarter 2023 dividend declaration.
